title: Ten Bets, One Bet
lede: Ten suppliers, each failing about one year in ten. How often do half of them fail together? It depends on one thing the supplier list does not show: whether they share a shock.

commit.title: YOUR NUMBER
commit.prompt: Ten suppliers, each failing about one year in ten. Out of 100 years, in how many do 5 or more of them fail in the same year?

captions: Each one fails about one year in ten.
Out of 100 years, how many see 5 or more of the ten fail?
Hold your number. The count will place it.
The AAA recipe: pool two loans, each fails one year in ten.
The top slice fails only if both fail: 1 year of 100.
Unless they fail together. Then it is 10 years of 100.
Moody's 2006 triple-A mortgage bonds: 83 of 100 downgraded.
Back to your ten. One row per year, 100 years.
No shared shock: 100 failures, scattered. Zero bad years.
Add one shared shock: about as many failures, in clumps.
Bad years per 100: 0.16 apart, 6.9 when they move together.
Monday: what one shock hits five of our ten at once?
Limits: these ρ are illustrative, not your suppliers'.

brand.takeaway: Ten bets that fail together are one bet.

sources: Coval, J. D., Jurek, J. W. & Stafford, E. (2009). The Economics of Structured Finance. Journal of Economic Perspectives 23(1), 3–25. doi:10.1257/jep.23.1.3 (the two-bond tranching example).

Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission (2011). The Financial Crisis Inquiry Report. US Government Printing Office. Conclusions of the Commission (Moody's 2006 triple-A mortgage securities: 83 % ultimately downgraded).
Salmon, F. (2009). Recipe for Disaster: The Formula That Killed Wall Street. Wired 17(03), 23 February 2009; reprinted in Significance 9(1), 16–20 (2012).
Li, D. X. (2000). On Default Correlation: A Copula Function Approach. Journal of Fixed Income 9(4), 43–54.
Vasicek, O. (2002). The Distribution of Loan Portfolio Value. Risk 15(12), 160–162 (the one-factor model used for every rate in the count).
honest: The shared-shock strengths ρ = 0.3 and 0.6 are illustrative, not measured for anyone's suppliers. The one-factor Gaussian copula is itself a mild model: real joint crashes are often worse than it says.

The hundred years on screen are one seeded draw (seed 630), chosen so its counts sit at the formula's rates (0, 3, 7 bad years); the rates come from the formula, not from the draw. A 10,000-year seeded check gives 0.14 %, 3.41 % and 7.11 %.

The mortgage example is Coval, Jurek and Stafford's stylised two-bond illustration of the AAA recipe, not one specific 2006 deal; the 83 of 100 downgrades had more than one cause, of which a nationwide fall in house prices, a shared shock, was the largest.

tryit.title: Try it
tryit.note: Turn the shared shock up or down; the same hundred years are re-thresholded.
